lab_table.hypothesis: Inclusion misses center on ~34px instances, smaller than the 0.3-0.7 pastes produced in R1 (which left inclusion AP flat at 0.355). Shrinking inclusion pastes to 0.3-0.5 (~27-45px from ~90px sources) should match the missed size band and lift inclusion AP50 above ~0.40 with improved low-tertile recall; if inclusion AP drops instead, 0.3-0.7 was already the sweet spot and scale is not the inclusion lever.

Inclusion is data-starved (10 real images, AP 0.355, recall 0.25) and R1's inclusion-heavy test was confounded by using default scale. Shifting budget to inclusion (24/13/13) while keeping the proven 0.3-0.7 small scale should raise inclusion AP50 above ~0.40 without dropping patches/scratches by more than ~0.03; if inclusion stays ~0.35, allocation is not the lever and the problem is purely scale/appearance.

Scratch AP fell 0.714->0.667 when pastes shrank to 0.3-0.7 (beyond the ~0.03 noise band), suggesting very small thin-line pastes are unlearnable noise, yet missed scratches (median 41.8px) are small. A mid scale 0.5-1.0 (~36-73px from ~73px sources) should recover scratch AP50 toward ~0.71 while keeping patches/inclusion at their proven 0.3-0.7; if scratches do not recover, the R1 drop was noise and per-class scale tuning is unnecessary.
CONTROL (added by the lab): repeat your last kept plan (allocation projected onto this round's constraints).

lesson: Inclusion-heavy allocation (24/13/13) at small scale 0.3-0.7 gave the best mAP (0.625) and best worst-class AP (0.3845) with inclusion recall up to 0.363 — inclusion is data-limited, so keep feeding it. Scratch mid-scale 0.5-1.0 was clearly worse (mAP 0.593, scratch AP did not recover), refuting 'small pastes hurt scratches' — keep scratches at 0.3-0.7. The control (repeat R1) swung wildly (patches 0.79->0.71, inclusion 0.35->0.41) at mAP 0.591, so per-class deltas under ~0.05 are noise; in the final round build on inclusion-heavy + 0.3-0.7 and avoid untested extreme allocations.
